assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme that reduces N2 to ammonia under ambient conditions, a problem of fundamental chemical mechanism with huge biological and agricultural importance. The field combines crystallography of the FeMo-cofactor (including the interstitial carbide), spectroscopy and kinetics of the electron-transfer/ATP-coupled cycle, and recent cryo-EM of turnover states. This is the type of mechanism-in-physical-terms biochemistry I value most.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallographic structure and cofactor architecture, Einsle resolved the central carbide and later structural states, and Seefeldt contributed the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Dean (genetics, biosynthesis) and Ribbe (cofactor assembly) are also credible, so priority and the three-person limit are a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed by multiple independent groups, but the catalytic mechanism at the cofactor (substrate binding site, hydride intermediates) is still debated. Recognition would be timely for the structural chemistry, though some might argue the mechanism is not yet closed.
uncertainties: Whether the E4 hydride/N2-binding mechanism is settled enough for a prize
Allocation of credit among Dean, Rees, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe is unresolved
I am relying on memory for details of recent cryo-EM turnover structures and have not verified them

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins established experimentally, with distance and driving-force dependence, how tunneling through the protein medium underlies respiration and photosynthesis. It ties Marcus theory to real biological machinery and is directly relevant to the physical principles of biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are a clear, compact pair with decades of defined experiments on ruthenium-modified proteins and hopping/tunneling pathways. Contributions of others (Beratan, Onuchic, Moser and Dutton) may be raised as theoretical and parallel experimental work, and Marcus already received the 1992 prize for the theory.
assessment.maturity: The core findings are old, thoroughly confirmed and widely taught, so maturity is not in question; the concern is that recognition is arguably late and that the 1992 prize may be seen as having covered the principle.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Marcus prize may reduce perceived novelty
Parallel contributions by Dutton and Moser need weighing against the supplied credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central concept for how enzymes (including respiratory oxidases and photosystem II) and molecular catalysts move protons and electrons together. The theory and model-system chemistry give a quantitative physical framework, and the work underlies artificial photosynthesis and water oxidation.
assessment.attribution: Mayer and Nocera made decisive experimental and conceptual contributions, Hammes-Schiffer the multistate theory; Meyer is also an important early contributor. The prize configuration is plausible but a line of work rather than one discovery, so allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: The concepts are widely adopted and independently verified in many systems. Quantitative links to enzyme mechanisms remain actively refined, so the field is mature but still evolving.
uncertainties: Whether this is one discovery or a broad conceptual line
Priority among Meyer, Mayer, Nocera and Hammes-Schiffer
Applicability of PCET models to complex enzymes is not fully settled

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view of protein folding turned Levinthal's paradox into a physical framework, and experimental mapping (phi-value analysis, engineered mutants) tested it. It is among the most significant conceptual advances in biophysical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the principal theorists of the funnel/minimal frustration view, with Fersht providing the experimental kinetics and transition-state mapping. Dill and Bryngelson have strong priority arguments, so the three-person cut would be contested.
assessment.maturity: The theory has been confirmed and extended for decades, including in structure prediction and design, so recognition is not premature. The 2024 prize for protein design/structure prediction may change the committee's view of how recent the field is.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between theory and experiment, and among Dill, Bryngelson, Wolynes and Onuchic
Possible perception that the 2024 prize already covers the protein-structure area

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation/dynamics methods made structure and motion of large biomolecules in solution accessible, including methyl-TROSY for very large complexes. They revealed dynamic mechanisms that static structures cannot, which is valuable for understanding enzymes.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore each have strong claims, with Palmer and Wagner also important. Wüthrich's 2002 prize covered the foundational structure determination, so the distinction of newer contributions must be made carefully.
assessment.maturity: Methods are fully mature, independently reproduced worldwide and in routine use. Timing is not premature; the question is relative priority against competing fields.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 Wüthrich prize
Choice of three among at least five credible contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase and gives stoichiometry, topology and ligand binding of intact protein complexes, including membrane proteins and respiratory-chain assemblies. It is a method that makes composition and dynamics visible and has had broad impact in structural biology.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is most associated with membrane protein complexes and instrument adaptation, Heck with development and application to large assemblies, and Chait with early biomolecular MS. Loo and Gross have legitimate earlier-method claims, and electrospray itself was recognized in 2002.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely adopted and independently confirmed. Interpretation of gas-phase structure retention has been debated but is now broadly accepted.
uncertainties: Whether gas-phase structures are faithful to solution structures remains a caveat
Priority among several contributors, and overlap with the 2002 electrospray prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation introduced a new organizing principle for cells and brought physical chemistry (polymer physics, multivalency) into cell biology. The conceptual impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne established P granules as liquid droplets, with Rosen providing the quantitative multivalency framework. Pappu and Mittag also made major contributions. It rests on a field-level shift more than on one sharply attributable discovery.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and still being debated regarding in vivo relevance, definitions of phase separation versus other assemblies and the functional consequences; this makes it more likely premature than the other choices.
uncertainties: Controversy about in vivo phase separation versus other mechanisms
Credit allocation among five credible contributors
Maturity is limited and the lasting mechanistic insight is not yet clear

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from microcrystals before radiation damage and time-resolved structural movies of reactions in proteins. It makes dynamic chemical mechanisms visible, matching my interest in time-resolved methods linked to structure.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the development of the method and the first demonstrations, Fromme the crystal and membrane protein samples, and Schlichting the time-resolved applications. Hajdu originated the diffraction-before-destruction idea, so priority is an issue.
assessment.maturity: Technique is confirmed at several facilities, but time-resolved results on reaction mechanisms are still accumulating and some interpretations have been challenged; recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the method has yet produced decisive mechanistic discoveries
Hajdu's priority versus the three-person limit
Facility-dependent reproducibility and artefact concerns in some time-resolved studies
